pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Southmead Primary School!
Our creative, inclusive and nurturing school is situated in Southfields, close to Wimbledon Common.
All our highly-skilled and dedicated staff members are committed to providing pupils with the highest quality of education and ensuring that they achieve their full potential. Our children are also aspirational for themselves and they love learning. Their unique talents and abilities, whether in sports, art, drama or music, are valued, celebrated and developed.
Throughout the school, our older pupils take pride in setting the younger children exceptional examples of behaviour and the very youngest pupils in the Early Years benefit from spacious outdoor learning areas and explorative learning experiences.
Southmead’s 18 place ASD base is a thriving hub of activity and learning. We are delighted to work with a range of specialist professionals to ensure the best progress for pupils with additional needs.
All pupils are encouraged to play an active role in the success of our school and to speak up, share their diverse opinions and make a difference. Pupil Voice Groups such as the Digital and Playground Leaders, and School Councillors represent and support their peers to with child-centred school improvement. Every voice is heard and our Head Boy and Head Girl provide strong role-models and further pupil leadership.
Southmead Primary pupils are always off on local trips or visiting places of educational interest such as the British Museum, the Houses of Parliament and London Zoo. Our range of clubs from Taekwondo to Dance to Science are very popular. Football training and well-being workshops with Fulham Football Club, as well as robotics classes with Chelsea FC, are highlights of the school year.
Pupil and staff well-being, as well as academic success, is a priority at Southmead Primary School and we are proud of our holistic approach to personal development, our accreditation as a “Flagship School” by the Inclusion Quality Mark (2025) and our “Good” Ofsted rating (2022).
Please feel welcome to visit our school and meet our dedicated staff and wonderful children. You will see the pupils’ positive attitudes towards learning, our broad and balanced curriculum and our values in action. You will also see why we are all so “Proud to Belong” at Southmead Primary School.

pageCache.text:
Our Values
Our school motto is Proud to Belong.
This relates to every area of school life – learning, teaching, behaviour, environment and atmosphere.
It means that every member of our school goes that “extra mile” to make the school the best it can be.
Southmead has a diverse community; all major world faiths are represented, and all cultures valued.
We have adopted 11 moral values which provide common understanding in school, and a framework from which to work in creating a cohesive atmosphere.
The values are broken down into a particular “Value of the Month” and provide a focus for assemblies and some parts of the curriculum.
Our Values of the Month:
October – Friendship
February – Thoughtfulness

Breakfast Club
Our breakfast club provides a safe, welcoming start to the day for children from Reception to Year 6.
When: 8:00 am – 8:40 am, Monday to Friday (term time only)
Cost: £3.20 per session
Please note: Breakfast club does not run on school closure days, school holidays, or during the first week back in September.
If your family is on a low income or receives free school meals, please speak with Miss Collier to discuss available support.
A Healthy Start to the Day.
We provide all our pupils with a nutritious breakfast to help them start their day ready to learn. Our menu consists of a varied selection of hot and cold healthy options.
After eating, children have the opportunity to take part in a range of fun educational activities and games that promote wellbeing and help them feel ready for the school day ahead.
Please call the office and they will send an application via ParentMail. It is important to note that parents/carers need to reapply for their child/ren’s spaces at breakfast club yearly. The office will send out applications in July for the next year.
At Southmead primary school we’re committed to ensuring every child starts the day ready to learn. Therefore, we provide a grab and go breakfast each morning to pupils as they arrive at school. We ensure that all children can enjoy a warm, buttered bagel or slice of toast when they arrive from 8:40 am.
A healthy breakfast helps children:
We’re proud to work with Magic Breakfast, a charity dedicated to ending child morning hunger, to provide this service to our school community.
Porridge

Our vision is that the whole school community learns about the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, that the school has a rights-respecting ethos and that the children are empowered to become active citizens and learners.

Governors
Meet the Governors and Committee Members of Southmead 2025/26
We offer you a warm welcome to our school at Southmead. We are very proud of the community that we are creating and believe that each child who comes to the school is treated as an individual and is helped to enjoy achieving the best they can using all the specialist resources we can provide.
At Southmead each child can thrive and learn to be part of a big community accessing extra clubs and activities that are a key part of what we are proud to offer and be able to take part in a range of opportunities and events including exhibitions and trips
We promise that each child in the school is valued as an individual and welcome the chance to look after and be part of the life journey of all who attend the school
Southmead Primary Governing Body
Roles within the Governing Body
The ChairThe Chair is elected by the Governing Body. Anyone who works at the school can not take the role of Chair. The Chair leads the Governor’s Meeting and carries out particular tasks, such as signing off the school budget.
The Vice-ChairThe Vice-Chair supports the Chair and he or she may be delegated specific tasks.
During the meetings, many aspects of the school are discussed, including:
This aspect sets the annual budget, monitors costs and authorises any major items of expenditure. It is also concerned with the maintenance and safety of the school buildings and grounds.
This aspect deals with curriculum matters and policies, the School Improvement Plan, assessment data and curriculum development and monitoring.
This area looks at areas such as staffing issues, appointments, redundancies, Performance Management and dismissals.
Our Governors usually meet as a Full Governing Body every half term. This is the meeting where all major decisions are made. However this is our minimum and sometimes it is necessary to meet more often, for example, when setting the budget. Our meetings start at 5:00 pm and are usually on a Thursday evening. They generally last between 2 and 3 hours, but this depends on the agenda and the matters which need to be discussed.

Teresa joined the Southmead governing body in December 2015 and is currently one of two of Southmead’s governing body Vice Chairs. Teresa has spent most of her working life at a consulting firm, advising clients and then running their learning and development team. As a governor, she has a particular interest in pupil assessment, attainment and progress.
I have been a governor since 2016 as a parent and then co-opted, with a brief stint as vice chair and now chair. I started my career in the corporate world in banking/financial administration. In the past decade or so I found my true passion which started in Mumbai doing pro bono consultancy for an edtech start up and working with grassroots educational projects which also included a stint teaching ESOL to underprivileged kids. I also have a MA in Development Education (global citizenship). Since moving back to England in 2016 I have worked for a large national charity with involved in the legal and safe running of a network of 116 volunteer run branches who offer peer support to their local communities. Finally I am the parent of 2 Southmead alumni who have both had very different needs and blossomed in ways I could not have expected under the care and guidance of the school.
Phillip joined the governing body in the summer of 2023, supporting Southmead as a finance governor. He is currently a risk consultant and internal auditor for financial services firms, working for a large professional services firm in Central London. Outside of his governor role at Southmead, Phillip volunteers his time every month to mentor Year 11 students in a secondary school in South East London. He has work experience in Washington, D.C. and also holds a Master’s degree in the History of International Relations. He currently lives in Shoreditch having previously spent several years in Wandsworth and Southwark.
Kieran joined the Southmead governing body in March 2024 as a co-opted governor. Kieran is a Chartered Accountant and Chartered Tax Advisor, working as a consultant at a professional services firm in Central London. He joined the firm as a school leaver in 2014 and is keen to use his experiences to work with the wider Southmead team. He currently lives in Balham, having lived in South West London for the previous 6 years.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Southmead Primary School, Princes Way, Wimbledon, SW19 6QT
pageCache.text:
Music
At Southmead, we want to create a passion for music in our pupils that will stay with them in their future lives. We want to ensure that music is an inspiring and engaging experience that enables every child to develop their full musical potential, whilst also developing an appreciation of the value of music that is deeply personal to them.
As a school, our intention is that children gain a strong understanding of what music is, in line with the National Curriculum, through: listening, singing, playing, evaluating, analysing, and composing across a wide variety of historical periods, traditions, styles and musical genres.
In Early Years, pupils build up skills that support listening, aural processing, communication, and rhythm through taking part in singing a range of songs, experimenting with sounds on instruments and exploring how the sounds can change. This equips our pupils with the vital skills they need in order to access the KS1 Music Curriculum.
By the end of KS1, our pupils will have developed confidence to sing with expression and explore songs, chants and rhythms creatively. They will have been introduced to a range of tuned and un-tuned instruments and use their knowledge of the interrelated dimensions to experiment and combine sounds. They will have been on a journey of exposure to a variety of live and recorded music from different genres and cultures.
In turn, this will prepare our children for their final Key Stage where they will be exposed to a range of music drawn from different traditions and historical composers. The listening skills they have built upon throughout their Primary schooling will result in them being able to listen with increasing attention to detail and aural memory. There will be a heavy focus on using instruments with control and fluency to compose and improvise using the interrelated dimensions they have been taught. At Southmead, our intent is that all pupils will leave for Secondary School being able to read, write and understand music notations in order to record their own compositions on a range of instruments.
Our objective at Southmead is to cultivate a curiosity for the subject, as well as an understanding and acceptance of the validity and importance of all types of music. We are committed to ensuring children understand the value and importance of music in the wider community, and are able to use their musical skills, knowledge, and experiences to involve themselves in music, in a variety of different contexts.
At Southmead, our Music Curriculum ties in heavily with our SMSC Values, ensuring that our children develop their self-esteem, creativity and cooperation skills that will in turn equip them with the skills for a life-long enjoyment of music.
It is evident through walk-arounds, lesson observation feedback and pupil voice, that our children are motivated to learn in lessons. Our Music Curriculum ensures that pupils are exposed to opportunities that involve singing, listening, playing, performing and evaluating. These skills are embedded in the weekly classroom Music lessons as well as the weekly singing assemblies, various concerts and performances, the learning of instruments, and the joining of one of our school choirs. Students that are identified as ‘More Able’ in Singing are encouraged to join a ‘More Able Choir’, where they learn a range of genres of songs that focus on skills such as harmonics, reading off notation sheet music. These pupils then participate regularly throughout the term in concerts for both the local community (for example Linden Lodge) and within school. Performances, such as Christmas plays and nativities and end of year shows, demonstrate that music is important to the life of the school. Extracurricular activities, such as choir also provide children with experience of making music.
The elements of music are taught in the classroom lessons so that children are able to use some of the language of music to dissect it, and understand how it is made, played, appreciated and analysed. In the classroom students across the school learn how to play a range of instruments, including wind, percussion and keyboards. Year 4 clarinet students participate in the Wandsworth Music Whole Class Teaching Program, learning the clarinet for an entire year.
Pupils are gaining more confidence in learning how to compose focusing on different dimensions of music, which in turn feeds their understanding when listening, playing, or analysing music. Composing or performing using body percussion and vocal sounds is also part of the curriculum, which develops the understanding of musical elements without the added complexity of an instrument.
In addition, our children are being exposed to a greater variety of historical composers from across different eras and genres through our introduction of “Composer of the Term”. Pupils learn in depth about their composer in Music lessons and focus on Listening & Analysis skills through their composer’s music. As per the new National Curriculum, Modern Composers and Artists have also been introduced to each class with the Composer of the term.
Our pupils will learn that music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. They will be inspired and engaged by their music education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Well being | Southmead Primary School, Princes Way, Wimbledon, SW19 6QT
pageCache.text:
Well being
The Department for Education (DfE) recognises that “in order to help their pupils succeed, schools have a role to play in supporting them to be resilient and mentally healthy”. Here at Southmead Primary School we embrace a whole school approach where all staff value and recognise the need to promote positive mental health and wellbeing in every child and adult.
We place great importance on developing the whole child academically, socially and emotionally. The skills needed throughout life can be taught and learnt at any age; all aspects of a child and young person’s experience in and out of school, contribute to their personal and social development and, as a school, we feel that it is essential that we share this role with parents, carers and families.
We are also extremely mindful of the wellbeing of all our staff who work at Southmead. We understand that stressed and anxious staff do not get the best out of their pupils and with this in mind we offer a variety of strategies to help our staff be healthy, in mind, body and spirit.
For more information about any support offered in school, please contact the school office.
Mrs Stagg (Headteacher) – Deputy DSL Mental Health First Aider
Miss Collier (DSL and Attendance Officer)
Mrs Furnell (Deputy Headteacher) – Mental Health First Aider
Miss Macarty – ELSA (Learning Mentor)
Miss Jacob – PSHE Lead
Mrs Joseph – PE Lead and Healthy Schools
Southmead Primary School has a multifaceted, proactive approach to supporting our children and their families, including:
All of the staff at Southmead Primary School play a fundamental role in the wellbeing of our pupils and their families.
BehaviourSelf-esteemAnger managementBereavementFamily breakdownsAnxietySocial communication
There will always be children and young people in schools facing life challenges that detract from their ability to engage with learning. Some will require greater support to increase their emotional literacy than others. ELSA is an initiative developed and supported by educational psychologists. It recognises that children learn better and are happier in school if their emotional needs are also addressed.
We are lucky enough to have a an Emotional Literacy Support Assistant at Southmead Primary. Mis Macarty has been trained by Educational Psychologists to plan and deliver programmes of support to pupils who are experiencing temporary or longer term additional emotional needs. The majority of ELSA work is delivered on an individual basis, but sometimes small group work is more appropriate, especially in the areas of social and friendship skills. Sessions are fun, we use a range of activities such as: games, role-play with puppets or arts and craft. ELSA sessions take place in our very own ‘Fir Room’ which provides a calm, safe space for the child to feel supported and nurtured.
Recognising emotions Self-esteem Social skills Friendship skills Anger management Loss and bereavement
Supporting – not fixing Remember, our school ELSA is not there to fix children’s problems. What she can do is provide emotional support. Our ELSA’s aim is to establish a warm, respectful relationship with a pupil and to provide a reflective space where they are able to share honestly their thoughts and feelings.

Special Education Needs and Disability (SEND)
Southmead’s Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) Hub
Our school motto, ‘Proud to Belong’, is at the heart of everything that we do at Southmead Primary School and inclusion and belonging is intrinsically embedded throughout our day to day school life.
In order to ensure that this is possible for all our pupils, including those with special educational needs, we make evidence based adaptations in order to support them. This is delivered through universal, targeted and specialist support.
Please see our 2026 SEND report for more information.
We use the Wandsworth Ordinarily Available Provision booklet to support our SEND provision across the school
At Southmead our Special Education Needs Co-ordinator (SENCo) is Nicolle Atkin. She has her NASENCo qualification. She can be contacted on 0208 788 8901.

For more information please also read the Accessibility Plan.
We have the following facilities available for pupils, parents or visitors with disabilities:
Accessibility plans and ‘reasonable adjustments’
The school seeks to make itself as accessible as it can possibly be to pupils with physical disabilities. Our accessibility plan sets out how the school intends to:
Understanding the curriculum
The school always aims to provide optimum access to the curriculum for pupils with special educational needs or physical disabilities.
We seek to look at the best way in which to help pupils access their learning in all areas and ensure that they have full access to a vibrant and engaging curriculum. We also seek to make any appropriate modifications to the physical environment of the school in order to ensure that all pupils are able to take part in all areas of learning. In Computing lessons for example, the school purchases keyboards and whiteboards which help pupils with particular needs access the curriculum and we may purchase software that connects words with pictures.
While the same basic rules apply to all children, the Education Authority can make a decision to provide transport on a case by case basis for a child with disabilities.
Your Education Authority region office will assess your child’s needs when making a decision, taking into account your child’s health and/or disability. If your child is offered school transport, the vehicle should have the relevant equipment to suit your child’s needs – for example wheelchair restraints, ramps or lifts.
For more detailed information about approved transport arrangement, please refer to your local Education Authority region office Transfer Booklet.
The Education Authority also provide escorts on school transport if needed. You may be able to get help with your own costs for taking your child to school. Your Education Authority region office will be able to advise you on these matters.
If your child cannot attend school for medical reasons
If your child cannot go to school because of medical needs or health problems, the Education Authority will be able to provide advice and guidance on how the needs of your child may be best met. Please find more information in our policies section.
The changes in the Children and Families Bill affect the way children with special educational needs (SEN) are supported in schools. The approach began in September 2014 and places pupils at the centre of planning. The key principles of the new legislation are:
1. Young people and their families should be involved in discussions about the support they need, so they can share their knowledge and feed back to the school on the young person’s progress.
2. Education, health and care plans (EHCP) will replace statements of special educational needs. New assessments for additional educational needs will follow the EHC guidelines from September 2014. (Existing statements will remain in force until all children and young people have completed the transition, which will be within three years).
3. School Action and School Action Plus will cease and be replaced by a single school-based category for children who need extra specialist support.

WAAS - Wandsworth Autistic Advisory Service
The Wandsworth Autism Advisory Service or WAAS for short is a single multi professional team that supports schools, settings and families in Wandsworth to achieve the best possible outcomes for children and young people with autism. The service supports education settings to enable all children with Autism/ social communication differences to achieve their full potential.
All parents with a child with autism/social communication difficulties, or those who are on the specialist pathway (undergoing a assessment for autism) can access this level of support.
What support is offered at this level?
Coffee Mornings – These are free for any parent of a CYP who has a diagnosis of autism (or is on the pathway for assessment). They provide a casual setting with no set agenda for parents to come and ask any questions and also share experiences with other parents.
Parent Workshops – These are events which are run by professionals within the WAAS team and will focus on a particular area of need. They will focus on understanding more about autism and offer strategies to support parenting with a space to ask questions at the end.
Every term, WAAS offer a range of parent workshops. Visit WAAS – Parents and Carers to find out what support may be on offer for you and your child.

Our Curriculum
“In a democratic society which prizes equality of opportunity, the curriculum should be based first and foremost on the knowledge we consider all young people should have the access to and begin to acquire during their school years.” Michael Young
How do we define curriculum?
“The bits I most remember about my school days are those that took place outside the classroom, as we were taken on countless theatre visits and trips to places of interest.” Alan Bennett
At Southmead we believe that curriculum refers to the ‘totality of the experience of the child within schooling (aims, content, pedagogy, assessment).’ This includes not just programmes of study, but wider experiences that include the development of the self, the healthy body and mind, the creative expression of individuals, in a way that impacts on a child’s long-term memory.
“The job of a good curriculum is to inspire teachers, not instruct them.” Russell Hobby
Here at Southmead, our biggest driving force is to ensure that we educate the ‘whole child’; by that we mean that we want them to achieve their potential in literacy and numeracy, but also seek to encourage a curiosity and enthusiasm across all subjects – a desire to know and understand more, building on prior learning, in a carefully sequenced progression. We aim to underpin our children’s learning with relevant practical experiences, where appropriate; drawing on the resources both locally and in London, to give our children new and invigorating experiences that will help embed their learning.
We believe that every child should:
be happy to come to school
understand and celebrate what they have achieved and know what they need to do next
have access to a curriculum that interests and motivates ; that builds curiosity, critical thinking and resilience, embedding a risk-taking attitude towards learning
be encouraged to work well with others, their school and embrace their diverse community
develop sound subject knowledge and be able to apply the appropriate skills across the curriculum, in different contexts
be able to make informed decisions about participation in wider society
have high aspirations for themselves, enabling greater life choices and experiences
If you would like to find out more about our curriculum, please contact our Curriculum Lead, Maxine Trace, through the School Office.

Relationships and Sex Education (RSE), and Health Education
Rationale for Relationships and Sex Education (RSE), and Health Education
Our pupils are growing up in an increasingly complex world: Advances in technology, whilst presenting many positive and exciting opportunities, pose considerable challenges and risks. Growing up in a diverse community also means that every pupil needs to learn how to show respect and care for every member of the school community regardless of beliefs, background, gender identity or culture. We support pupils to reflect and think about the way values, Rights of the Child (UNCRC), beliefs, attitudes and behaviours affect people’s lives including theirs, that of the community and the wider world.
Everyone faces difficult situations in their lives, and growing up can be hard. At Southmead we want our pupils to develop their resilience, so that they know how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way; we want our pupils to develop knowledge that will enable them to make informed decisions about their well-being and know where to access support when they need it. Relationships and Sex Education, and Health Education is lifelong learning and we teach it so that our pupils grow up to become happy, healthy, responsible, safe and successful adults of the future.

Playground Leaders
Playground Leaders take part in training to develop leadership skills which they use to lead others in sports activities. They have learnt how to communicate effectively, be organised, take responsibility and work with other people; all core skills which are important throughout life. Selected leaders support in the dining hall at lunchtimes by helping to serve water to pupils and help encourage manners and keeping the space tidy for others. In the playground, they organise a variety of games and activities for their peers to take part in. Additional responsibilities include supporting lunchtime competitions, writing reports for the newsletter and helping out at afterschool clubs.
Playground Buddies
Here at Southmead we are a Rights Respecting School and we all have the right to express our views and feelings and to be listened to. Children in Year 4 and 5 have trained to become Playground Buddies. Training includes communication and listening skills, team building, working together, problem solving using Kelso’s Choices and confidentiality. They are available at lunchtimes to listen and support their peers, giving them an opportunity to talk to about any worries or problems in a safe place.
The training is supported by the ChildLine in Partnerships (CHIPS) programme and all Playground Buddies receive ongoing support from staff within the school.

Art & Design
Our intent at Southmead is to deliver the art and design National Curriculum in a rich and varied way. We teach a broad range of skills and techniques through six content areas: drawing, painting, printing, textiles, sculpture and digital media which enables a steady progression from foundation to Year 6. In this way the children become proficient in a wide range of techniques and gain knowledge about how art, craft and design are applied in the world. Children learn to evaluate their own work and appreciate the work of others which fosters a sense of equality and celebrates effort and creativity. They develop resilience and resourcefulness and skills that will support their wellbeing throughout their lives.Children’s work is recorded in sketch books and is celebrated across the school in displays.
Art and Design is taught by a specialist in KS1 and KS2. Lessons follow the knowledge and skills content as laid out in the National Curriculum. Targets are set for each year group and these are used for the long and medium term plans. The plans are closely linked to the school picture curriculum map to ensure that art and design compliments learning in other subjects and that cross curricular links are made wherever possible.
Lessons are carefully structured to cover the different disciplines of drawing, painting, printing, 3D modelling, textiles and collage through the year. By Year 6 children have experienced a rich and very diverse range of techniques that build and widen skills from prior learning.
Each lesson starts with a short power point that introduces relevant artists, designers or techniques. The learning objective and appropriate UN Rights Respecting Schools article are explained. The activities are carefully broken down into manageable steps which are explained in a demonstration. The aim is to build independence, confidence and an ability to work for longer periods of time on a piece of work. Research and planning is done in sketch books. Teaching Assistants support children by working alongside, demonstrating the techniques. Work is shared and appreciated throughout the lesson. Two artists of the week are chosen at the end of the lesson. This tends to be based on effort and who has been a good role model.
The lessons are engaging and challenging and the five R’s are frequently referred to. Resilience is always encouraged. The aim throughout is to develop fine motor skills, visual awareness and creativity. Links to other subjects and to the wider world are made whenever possible.
Children work in sketch books and on paper for drawing and painting. Work is displayed around the school and the aim is to ensure that all children have their work on display at some stage in the year.
